items: Draw your personal dating pipeline by listing every action you take between opening an app and going on a date, including habits like scrolling Instagram first or rewording messages before sending, because making your invisible habits visible is the first step toward changing them.

Write down all seven stages of the dating pipeline—open app, swipe, get matched, send opening message, back-and-forth conversation, date scheduling, and the actual date—so you can see exactly where your time is going.

Document each specific behavior in your pipeline from opening the app to scheduling a date, because the gap between what you think you do and what you actually do is where your energy disappears without you noticing.

Identify the decision points in your pipeline where you can either continue forward or redirect your effort, because understanding where you have choices gives you control over how much energy you spend.
Calculate your conversion rate at each pipeline stage by tracking how many people out of every 100 progress to the next step, because knowing your real numbers exposes where your effort is wasted.
Track your actual numbers like matches, messages, and scheduled dates instead of guessing how you're performing, because feelings about dating are unreliable but real data never lies.
Count only stages 6 and 7 (date scheduling and the date itself) as true outcomes, since everything before that is preparation that produces no results regardless of how many matches you have.
Find where you're spending energy without getting dates by comparing how much time you invest in each stage against your conversion rates, because you might be grinding at the wrong steps.
Set time limits for stages 4 and 5 (opening messages and back-and-forth conversation) to prevent unlimited chatting from exhausting you before any actual dates happen.
Choose how much effort to spend at each stage based on your conversion rates instead of defaulting to the app's design, which wants you stuck in stages 2 and 5 forever.
Build a scheduling system that moves conversations to actual dates within a set number of messages, because indefinite messaging lets conversations die and prevents you from meeting people.

Set boundaries on how many hours per week you spend in the app and cap how many messages you exchange before asking someone out, so you stay in control of your dating effort instead of letting the apps consume your time.
